note: Every entry below was verified against the vendor's own source on 2026-09-19 by two independent passes. Availability is not authorization: an agent may use a server only within the permission the user has already given, and a mutating call still stops and asks. Nothing here is installed by this repository.

servers.name: Workspace files and terminal
servers.purpose: Read, search and edit files in the project, and run commands.
servers.source: Built into the host runtime (Claude Code: Read/Write/Edit/Grep/Glob/Bash). Not an MCP server and nothing to install.
servers.auth: none — governed by the runtime's permission mode
servers.read_only_option: The runtime's permission mode; a read-only role simply does not call the mutating tools.
servers.notes: Listed so loadouts can name it explicitly. It is the baseline every other entry is measured against.

servers.name: GitHub MCP Server
servers.purpose: Repositories, files, issues, pull requests, commits, Actions and code search as an authoritative source of repository state.
servers.transport: remote https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/ (OAuth or PAT); local ghcr.io/github/github-mcp-server via Docker
servers.auth: GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN, or OAuth against the remote endpoint
servers.read_only_option: --read-only flag; GITHUB_TOOLSETS scopes which of the 22 toolsets are exposed at all
servers.activation: The task needs repository state that is not on local disk — issues, PRs, CI runs, another repo.
servers.fallback: git and the gh CLI against the local checkout; say which repository facts could not be confirmed.
servers.notes: Prefer --read-only for review and audit roles. Writing an issue, a PR or a comment is an outward-facing action and needs its own confirmation.

servers.name: Playwright MCP
servers.purpose: Drive a real browser: navigate, screenshot, interact, emulate viewports, read console and network.
servers.auth: none by default; a persistent profile carries whatever the browser is logged into
servers.read_only_option: None. --isolated gives an in-memory profile and is the real containment control.
servers.activation: Rendered behaviour has to be observed rather than inferred — UI work, a browser-only bug, Core Web Vitals.
servers.fallback: The host's own browser tools, or a local Playwright script. With neither, report that rendered verification was unavailable and never describe the UI as verified.
servers.notes: Its README states plainly: "Playwright MCP is not a security boundary." --allowed-origins is NOT a security control either — the README says it "does not serve as a security boundary and does not affect redirects". A non-isolated profile can act as the logged-in user on any site.

servers.name: Context7
servers.purpose: Fetch current, version-aware documentation for a library or framework instead of relying on stale model knowledge.
servers.auth: API key for higher rate limits; usable without one
servers.read_only_option: read-only by nature — its tools are resolve-library-id and query-docs
servers.activation: A framework or library API matters and its current behaviour is not knowable from the repository.
servers.fallback: Official documentation via the browser; cite what was read.
servers.notes: Do not reach for it to answer questions the repository already answers. Library entries are community-contributed, so treat a returned snippet as evidence to check, not as authority.

servers.name: Figma MCP Server
servers.purpose: Inspect design files, components, variables and design tokens, and compare an implementation against the design.
servers.license: proprietary — hosted service, no public repository
servers.auth: Figma account; the remote server is available on all seats and plans, the desktop server needs a Dev or Full seat on a paid plan
servers.read_only_option: Use only the read tools (get_design_context, get_metadata, get_screenshot, get_variable_defs and the rest); the write and Weave tool groups change or generate canvas content.
servers.activation: The task references a Figma file or a design system held in Figma, and the server is configured.
servers.fallback: Work from the repository's own design tokens, existing components and screenshots. Never invent what a design says.
servers.notes: Three tool groups: read, write, and Weave (which runs tools and uploads assets). Figma for Government supports only the desktop server — the remote one is not available there, and MCP is outside Figma's FedRAMP audit scope.

servers.name: Supabase MCP
servers.purpose: Inspect and operate a Supabase project — schema, SQL, edge functions, logs, advisors.
servers.transport: hosted https://mcp.supabase.com/mcp; local via the Supabase CLI at http://localhost:54321/mcp
servers.auth: Supabase personal access token or project credentials
servers.read_only_option: Point it at a local or branch project rather than production, and prefer its read-only mode where the deployment offers one.
servers.activation: The project actually uses Supabase — supabase/ directory, a Supabase client dependency, or the user says so.
servers.fallback: Read migrations and schema files from the repository; state that live database state was not inspected.
servers.notes: The repository was renamed from supabase-community/supabase-mcp to supabase/mcp; the old URL still redirects. Never assume production access — apply migrations to a branch or local project first.

servers.name: Vercel MCP
servers.purpose: Inspect Vercel projects, deployments, logs and configuration, and run Vercel CLI operations.
servers.license: proprietary — hosted service, no public repository
servers.auth: OAuth against the user's Vercel account
servers.read_only_option: none published — scope by using only the inspection tools
servers.activation: The project deploys to Vercel — vercel.json, a linked project, or the user says so.
servers.fallback: Read vercel.json and CI configuration from the repository; treat deployment state as unknown.
servers.notes: Vercel's own documentation says connecting "grants the AI system you're using the same access as your Vercel user account", and its purchase tools "execute real, non-refundable charges". Deployment and purchase are separately authorized actions — preparing a deployment is not permission to run one.

servers.name: Reference Postgres MCP server (archived)
servers.purpose: Recorded so nobody adds it: the Model Context Protocol reference Postgres server is no longer maintained.
servers.fallback: For Supabase projects use the supabase entry. Otherwise use psql and the project's own migration tooling through the workspace, and keep production credentials out of the agent's reach.
servers.notes: It was removed from modelcontextprotocol/servers and moved to servers-archived. Any guide still recommending it is stale.

servers.name: Cloudflare MCP servers
servers.purpose: Cloudflare account and platform: API/config, docs, observability, Workers builds and bindings, Radar, browser rendering.
servers.license: Apache-2.0 (repo); the endpoints are a hosted Cloudflare service
servers.transport: Remote, one endpoint per server. Main API: https://mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp; docs: https://docs.mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp; observability: https://observability.mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp
servers.auth: OAuth with per-permission consent, or a scoped Cloudflare API token as a bearer header
servers.read_only_option: No flag. Contain it by granting narrow permissions at the OAuth screen or minting a read-only API token.
servers.activation: The project runs on Cloudflare — wrangler.toml, Workers, Cloudflare DNS — and the server is configured.
servers.fallback: Read wrangler.toml and CI config from the repository; treat live edge state as unknown.
servers.notes: The main API server is read AND write over 2,500+ endpoints including DNS, Workers and Zero Trust. The docs and observability endpoints are the safe ones. Container and Browser Run endpoints spend billable resources.

servers.name: Sentry MCP
servers.purpose: Inspect issues, events, traces and releases; triage.
servers.license: FSL-1.1-Apache-2.0 (Functional Source License, Apache-2.0 future licence)
servers.auth: Sentry OAuth; the documented scopes include write scopes (project:write, team:write, event:write)
servers.read_only_option: None published. Scope the endpoint to one org/project and keep to inspection tools.
servers.activation: The project uses Sentry and an error or regression needs real production evidence.
servers.fallback: Application logs through the workspace; say that production error data was not available.
servers.notes: Sentry describes it as "primarily designed for human-in-the-loop coding agents". docs.sentry.io/product/sentry-mcp/ now redirects to mcp.sentry.dev.

servers.name: Grafana MCP
servers.purpose: Query Prometheus/Loki, read dashboards and alerts, inspect incidents and profiles.
servers.transport: Local: uvx mcp-grafana, docker grafana/mcp-grafana, or go install
servers.read_only_option: Disable the write-capable tool groups; 29+ tools are enabled by default.
servers.activation: The project's observability lives in Grafana and a question needs real telemetry.
servers.fallback: Logs and metrics reachable from the workspace; state what was not observed.
servers.notes: Default tool set can create and update dashboards, alert rules, annotations and incidents — that is production observability config, not just reads.

servers.name: Datadog MCP
servers.purpose: Query metrics, logs, traces, monitors and incidents.
servers.license: MIT on the datadog-labs examples repo; the server itself is Datadog-hosted
servers.read_only_option: Permission-scoped: Datadog checks the matching permission (e.g. monitors_write) on each tool call, so a read-only key yields a read-only server.
servers.activation: The project's telemetry is in Datadog and the question needs production evidence.
servers.fallback: Whatever telemetry is reachable locally; say what could not be observed.
servers.notes: Datadog does publish an official managed MCP server, contrary to a common assumption. The public repo under datadog-labs holds docs and examples, not the server.

servers.name: Linear MCP
servers.purpose: Find, create and update issues, projects and comments.
servers.read_only_option: A purpose-built read-only endpoint: https://mcp.linear.app/mcp/readonly — use it unless the task genuinely requires filing or editing issues.
servers.activation: The team tracks work in Linear and the task needs issue context.
servers.fallback: Work from what the user pasted or from the repository's own issue references.
servers.notes: The only server in this catalog shipping a dedicated read-only endpoint. Creating or updating an issue is outward-facing and needs confirmation.

servers.name: Notion MCP
servers.purpose: Search, read, create and update Notion pages and databases.
servers.license: hosted service not published; the self-hosted server is MIT
servers.auth: Notion OAuth, or NOTION_TOKEN for the self-hosted server
servers.read_only_option: None. Restrict by sharing only the pages the integration needs.
servers.activation: The team's docs or specs live in Notion and the task needs them.
servers.fallback: Ask for the content, or work from the repository's own docs.
servers.notes: Write tools create, update, move and duplicate pages and databases — shared workspace content. Some tools are plan-gated. Self-hosted v2.0.0 was a breaking change: database tools became data-source tools.

servers.name: Slack MCP
servers.purpose: Read channels and threads, search history, and send messages.
servers.auth: Slack OAuth; workspace admins approve MCP client integrations
servers.read_only_option: None. Keep to search and read tools.
servers.activation: The task genuinely needs Slack content, and the workspace admin has approved the integration.
servers.fallback: Ask the user to paste the thread.
servers.notes: The highest-consequence server here: it sends messages to real people, creates canvases and uploads files. Every send is an outward-facing action requiring explicit per-message confirmation — drafting is not sending.

servers.name: Google Workspace MCP servers
servers.purpose: Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Chat and People as first-party MCP endpoints.
servers.transport: One remote endpoint per product, e.g. Gmail https://gmailmcp.googleapis.com/mcp/v1, Drive https://drivemcp.googleapis.com/mcp/v1
servers.activation: The user has connected the specific product and the task needs it.
servers.fallback: Ask the user for the content; never guess at the contents of a mailbox or calendar.
servers.notes: Google now publishes first-party Workspace MCP servers (Developer Preview) — community servers are no longer the only option and should not be used in preference. Google's own docs warn that these clients have powerful access and should be treated accordingly. Sending mail or creating events is outward-facing: confirm each one.

servers.name: Chrome DevTools MCP
servers.purpose: Drive Chrome with DevTools access: performance traces, network, console, DOM, plus full interaction.
servers.auth: none; a non-isolated profile carries the user's logins
servers.read_only_option: None. It clicks, fills, uploads and evaluates scripts.
servers.activation: The question needs DevTools-grade evidence — a performance trace, detailed network timing — beyond what plain browser control gives.
servers.fallback: The playwright MCP or the host's own browser tools.
servers.notes: Official Google/Chrome. Strongest choice for performance profiling of a real page; overlaps playwright for plain interaction.

servers.name: axe DevTools MCP (Deque)
servers.purpose: Automated accessibility scanning with code-level remediation guidance.
servers.transport: Docker or npm, per Deque's documentation
servers.read_only_option: Use its scan tools without acting on the remediate tool's edits automatically.
servers.activation: Accessibility must be checked and the organization has axe DevTools.
servers.fallback: axe-core via the browser or @axe-core/playwright, plus the manual keyboard and screen-reader checks a scanner cannot make.
servers.notes: Official Deque server. Its remediate tool produces code changes — review them, do not apply blind. An automated scan catches roughly a third of WCAG issues: it never proves accessibility on its own.

servers.name: Postgres MCP (community alternatives)
servers.purpose: Generic Postgres access where no vendor server applies.
servers.transport: Local: pipx install postgres-mcp / uvx postgres-mcp / docker crystaldba/postgres-mcp
servers.read_only_option: --access-mode=restricted. The default is not unrestricted, but confirm the mode before pointing it anywhere real.
servers.activation: Only with the user's explicit say-so, against a local or throwaway database.
servers.fallback: psql through the workspace against a local database, and the repository's migrations as the schema source of truth.
servers.notes: NOT official — published by Crystal DBA, an independent company. It is the most-cited successor to the archived reference server, but it is a third party holding a database connection string. Never point it at production. For Neon, Neon publishes its own official server (https://neon.com/docs/ai/neon-mcp-server), which its own docs warn grants broad database management.
